title: Dual-number tangent vectors form a vector space
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $x\in X$ a point with residue field $\kappa=\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and $\kappa[\epsilon]$ the dual numbers over $\kappa$ [def-sc-dual-numbers]. Let $\kappa[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]$ be the $\kappa$-algebra with basis $1,\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2$ and $\epsilon_1^2=\epsilon_1\epsilon_2=\epsilon_2^2=0$. For $i=1,2$ let $j_i:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon]\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the $\kappa$-algebra map with $\epsilon_i\mapsto\epsilon$, $\epsilon_{3-i}\mapsto0$, let $s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon]\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]$ be $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the $\kappa$-algebra map with $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\mapsto\epsilon$, and let $c:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon]$ be $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the map $\epsilon\mapsto0$. Let $T$ be the set of morphisms of $k$-schemes $\theta:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon]\to X$ with $\theta\circ c$ equal to the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ at $x$. Then: (a) the commutative square $j_1\circ c=j_2\circ c$ is a pushout in the category of schemes, so for $\theta_1,\theta_2\in T$ there is a unique morphism of schemes $\Theta:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]\to X$ with $\Theta\circ j_i=\theta_i$ for $i=1,2$, and $\Theta$ is a morphism of $k$-schemes; (b) $\theta_1+\theta_2:=\Theta\circ s$ and, for $\lambda\in\kappa$, $\lambda\theta:=\theta\circ\operatorname{Spec}(m_\lambda)$, where $m_\lambda$ is the $\kappa$-algebra endomorphism of $\kappa[\epsilon]$ with $\epsilon\mapsto\lambda\epsilon$, are elements of $T$, and these operations make $T$ a $\kappa$-vector space whose zero element is the composite of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon]\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ (induced by $\kappa\to\kappa[\epsilon]$) with the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$.

proof.text: For $\theta_1,\theta_2\in T$ we have $\theta_1\circ c=\theta_2\circ c$, both being the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. The dual-number pushout [lem-sc-dual-number-scheme-pushout] with $K=\kappa$ and $n=2$ gives a unique morphism $\Theta:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]\to X$ with $\Theta\circ j_i=\theta_i$; this is (a) except the last clause. Composing $\Theta$ with the structure morphism $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, both $p\circ\Theta$ and the structure morphism of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]$ restrict along $j_i$ to the structure morphism of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon]$, so they agree by the uniqueness in the same statement (target $\operatorname{Spec}k$); hence $\Theta$ is a morphism of $k$-schemes.

The composite $\Theta\circ s$ restricts along $c$ to the common base point because $j_1\circ c=j_2\circ c=s\circ c$. Likewise, precomposition by $\operatorname{Spec}(m_\lambda)$ preserves the base point because $m_\lambda$ fixes the quotient map $\epsilon\mapsto0$. Thus the displayed addition and scalar multiplication are closed on $T$, and the constant map through $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ is the zero element.

Each identity is checked by writing both sides as $\Psi\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ for a $\kappa$-algebra map $\varphi:\kappa[\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n]\to\kappa[\epsilon]$ and comparing restrictions along the $j_i$, using the uniqueness in [lem-sc-dual-number-scheme-pushout] with $K=\kappa$ and $n=2$ or $n=3$. For $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n\in T$ let $\Theta_n$ be the unique morphism from $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n]$ restricting to $\theta_i$ along $j_i$. Associativity: both $(\theta_1+\theta_2)+\theta_3$ and $\theta_1+(\theta_2+\theta_3)$ equal $\Theta_3\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3\mapsto\epsilon)$, since e.g. the map $\Theta_3\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\mapsto\epsilon_1,\ \epsilon_3\mapsto\epsilon_2)$ from $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]$ restricts to $\theta_1+\theta_2$ and $\theta_3$ along $j_1,j_2$ (the first by uniqueness for $n=2$), so it is the $\Theta$ of that pair. Commutativity: $\Theta_2\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon_1\leftrightarrow\epsilon_2)$ is the $\Theta$ of $(\theta_2,\theta_1)$, and the swap fixes $s$. Zero: for $\theta_2=0$, $\Theta_2=\theta_1\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon\mapsto\epsilon_1)$, so $\theta_1+0=\theta_1$. Scalars: $\lambda\theta+\mu\theta=\theta\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon\mapsto(\lambda+\mu)\epsilon)$ because the pair $(\lambda\theta,\mu\theta)$ glues to $\theta\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon\mapsto\lambda\epsilon_1+\mu\epsilon_2)$; similarly $\lambda(\theta_1+\theta_2)=\lambda\theta_1+\lambda\theta_2$ via $\epsilon_i\mapsto\lambda\epsilon_i$, $(\lambda\mu)\theta=\lambda(\mu\theta)$ and $1\theta=\theta$ since $m_\lambda m_\mu=m_{\lambda\mu}$ and $m_1=\mathrm{id}$, and $\theta+(-1)\theta=\theta\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon\mapsto0)$, which is the zero element. Each such $\varphi$ is a $\kappa$-algebra map because all products of the $\epsilon_i$ vanish.
